title: Pane di Matera
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A protected, distinctively shaped durum wheat bread from Matera, its thick, deeply cracked crust and dense crumb the result of a long natural fermentation and traditional wood-fired baking.
longDesc: Pane di Matera holds an official protected geographical status, its shape historically stamped with a family seal before being sent to communal ovens, and the bread's exceptionally long shelf life once made it a practical staple for the region's farming families.
ingredients: 500 g (3⅓ cups) durum wheat semolina flour
10 g (2 tsp) active dry yeast (or a natural starter)
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm water and let sit for 5 minutes.
Combine the semolina flour and salt, then add the yeast mixture, kneading for 12–15 minutes until smooth and elastic — durum dough requires more kneading than standard wheat.
Let rise, covered, for at least 4–6 hours at room temperature, or ideally overnight in the refrigerator for a slower, more flavorful fermentation.
Shape the dough into its traditional horn or double-lobed shape.
Let rise again for about 1–1.5 hours until nearly doubled.

Score the top deeply and bake at 230°C (450°F) with steam (a pan of water in the oven) for the first 15 minutes, then reduce to 200°C (400°F) for another 40–45 minutes until deeply golden with a thick, cracked crust.
Cool completely on a wire rack before slicing.
chefTips: Durum semolina dough needs more kneading than standard wheat flour to develop proper structure.
A long, slow fermentation is what develops the bread's characteristic depth of flavor.
Steam in the oven during the initial bake helps develop the bread's thick, deeply cracked crust.
commonMistakes: Underkneading the dense durum dough, resulting in a poorer structure.
Rushing the fermentation, which misses much of the bread's traditional flavor development.
Skipping the steam step, resulting in a thinner, less characterful crust.
servedWith: As an accompaniment to any meal
storage: Store at room temperature for up to a week — this bread is known for keeping unusually well.
reheating: Refresh briefly in the oven if it has softened.
healthBenefits: A naturally vegan bread, with durum wheat providing more protein than standard wheat flour.
culturalNote: Pane di Matera holds a protected geographical status, its distinctive shape and exceptional keeping quality reflecting centuries of tradition in the historic city of Matera.
